pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: In your own words: what is a language server, and why is it a separate program rather than part of the editor?
expected_points: a separate program that understands one specific language
the editor sends it the file/cursor state and displays its answers: diagnostics, completions, go-to-definition, hover
separation via a shared protocol means any editor can use any language's server

questions.prompt: You've installed a language extension for a new language. How would you check the editor actually understands your file, rather than just displaying text?
expected_points: introduce a deliberate mistake and expect a diagnostic squiggle / Problems entry
trigger completions and expect legal, context-aware suggestions
go-to-definition (F12) or hover works on a name

questions.prompt: You need a file whose name you half-remember, buried deep in a big project, and then you forget the shortcut for a command you need. What do you reach for in each case, instead of the mouse?
expected_points: quick open (Cmd/Ctrl+P) with fuzzy matching finds the file by partial name
the command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P) finds any command by name
the palette shows shortcuts, so it replaces memorizing them

questions.prompt: A friend asks whether to use a full IDE or VS Code for (a) their first months learning to program across a couple of languages, and (b) full-time work in one huge single-language codebase. What do you advise, and why?
expected_points: lightweight editor for (a): fast, free, one tool across languages, less overwhelming
an IDE is defensible for (b): deepest single-language analysis and tooling out of the box
the justification is fit-for-task trade-offs (setup effort, resources, cost, depth), not a universal best

questions.prompt: Five editors, ten languages. How many integrations does the world need with editor-specific plugins, and how many with the Language Server Protocol? Why did that arithmetic win?
expected_points: without a protocol: 5 x 10 = 50 integrations; with LSP: 5 + 10 = 15
each editor implements the protocol once, each language ships one server
so even niche editors get first-class language support

questions.prompt: When would you pick multi-cursor over find-and-replace-all, and when the reverse?
expected_points: multi-cursor: you confirm each edit site visually as you add selections, and can make edits that differ per cursor position
replace-all: better for many occurrences across files, but can silently hit unintended matches
